SQL Editor

A superuser-only workspace for running SQL and managing PocketBase collections and fields. No prior SQL experience required — this page explains everything step by step.

Opening the SQL Editor

  1. Log in to the Dashboard as a superuser (an admin-style account).
  2. Open Collections in the left sidebar.
  3. Click the SQL Editor button (the terminal icon) at the bottom of the sidebar.

You can also go directly to /_/#/collections/sql-editor.

The SQL Editor is only visible to superusers. Regular app users can never open it.

Quick start

Type a query in the editor and press Ctrl+Enter (or Cmd+Enter on macOS):

SELECT * FROM posts;

The results appear in a table below the editor. If the table has image/file columns they are shown as thumbnails (see Results).

  • Every statement ends with a semicolon ;.
  • Query strings in this editor are case-insensitive — select and SELECT are the same.
  • Queries that change data ask for confirmation before running.
  • Only superusers can run anything here, so use it carefully.

How statements are handled

Most statements run as raw SQL. A few are translated into native PocketBase operations so that your schema stays consistent (visible in the Collections sidebar, the REST API, filters, relations, and so on).

StatementWhat happens
SELECT ...Raw query. Results are shown in a table below the editor (max 1000 rows).
INSERT / UPDATE / DELETERaw execution. The number of affected rows is reported.
CREATE TABLE ...Creates a native PocketBase collection (with native fields).
DROP TABLE ...Deletes the matching native collection (falls back to raw SQL otherwise).
ALTER TABLE ... ADD COLUMNAdds a native field to an existing collection.
ALTER TABLE ... DROP COLUMNRemoves a native field from an existing collection.
Everything elseExecuted as raw SQL (PRAGMA, ANALYZE, VACUUM, etc.).
Why does this matter? If you created tables with plain SQLite, the Dashboard would not know about them. By turning CREATE TABLE / ALTER TABLE into native PocketBase operations, the created collections show up everywhere in the app, just as if you had created them through the Dashboard UI.

Writing and running queries

Run everything

  • Click the Run button (the play icon) in the page header, or
  • press Ctrl+Enter / Cmd+Enter inside the editor.

Run only part of the editor

This is handy when you have several statements and only want to test one of them.

  1. Highlight (select) the text you want to run.
  2. Click Run — when text is selected the button label changes to Run Selected — or press Ctrl+Enter.

You can also click the small arrow (▾) next to the Run button to open a menu with two choices:

  • Run — runs the whole editor.
  • Run Selected — runs only the highlighted text. This option is greyed out until you highlight something.
Selecting text and running only that selection does not change what is stored in the editor — the full query stays in place after the selection finishes running.

Editor keyboard shortcuts

ShortcutAction
Ctrl+Enter / Cmd+EnterRun the query (or the selection, if any)
Ctrl+/Comment / uncomment the current line or selection (see below)
Ctrl+ZUndo
Ctrl+Y or Ctrl+Shift+ZRedo
Ctrl+LSelect the current line
Ctrl+DSelect the word at the cursor
TabIndent the current line / selection
Shift+TabUn-indent the current line / selection
EscLeave the editor
The editor keeps its own undo history, so Ctrl+Z / Ctrl+Y work reliably even after commenting, indenting or using autocomplete.

Comments

Comments are notes that the database ignores. Use them to explain your queries or to temporarily disable a statement.

Single line: press Ctrl+/ with the cursor on one line (or a selection inside a single line). The line is prefixed with //:

// SELECT * FROM posts;

Multiple lines: highlight more than one line and press Ctrl+/. The whole block is wrapped in a /* ... */ comment:

/* CREATE TABLE images (
    posts TEXT,
    avatar FILE,
    images FILE,
    interests SELECT(football, Gaming, Coding)
); */

Press Ctrl+/ again on the same text to remove the comment.

Creating collections

Use CREATE TABLE to create a new collection:

CREATE TABLE posts (
    title TEXT,
    content TEXT,
    views INTEGER DEFAULT 0
);

Because CREATE TABLE produces a native collection, posts immediately appears in the Collections sidebar and is available through the Records API.

PocketBase automatically adds the system fields id, created and updated to every collection, so you do not need to define them yourself.

PocketBase field types

Besides the standard SQL types, column definitions may use PocketBase-specific type keywords so you can create any field type supported by the Dashboard:

KeywordField typeOptions / example
TEXT(500)Plain textoptional max length
EDITOR / RICH / HTMLRich text editor
NUMBER, INTEGER, REALNumberINTEGER is integer-only
BOOL / BOOLEANBool
EMAILEmail
URLURL
DATE / DATETIMEDate
AUTODATEAutodateauto set on create
FILEFile
RELATION(collection)RelationRELATION(posts), optional max select as 2nd arg
SELECT(a,b,c)Selectcomma separated values
JSONJSON
GEOPOINT / GEOGeo Point
PASSWORDPassword

Constraints such as NOT NULL and PRIMARY KEY are recognised and mapped to the field required option.

CREATE TABLE articles (
    title TEXT NOT NULL,
    cover FILE,
    author RELATION(users),
    status SELECT(draft, published),
    tags SELECT(news, tech, life),
    location GEOPOINT,
    meta JSON,
    published_at AUTODATE
);

Altering collections

-- add a native field
ALTER TABLE articles ADD COLUMN summary TEXT;

-- add a PocketBase specific field
ALTER TABLE articles ADD COLUMN thumbnail FILE;

-- remove a field
ALTER TABLE articles DROP COLUMN summary;

System fields (id, created, updated) cannot be removed.

Dropping collections

DROP TABLE articles;
Dropping a collection also deletes all of its records. This cannot be undone.

Results

SELECT results are rendered in a table below the editor:

  • The id column is always shown first, no matter where it is in your query.
  • Click a column header to sort the results by that column (click again to reverse).
  • Only the first 250 rows are shown at first. If there are more, a Load remaining button appears at the bottom of the table. At most 1000 rows are returned per query.
  • A Export as CSV button appears below the table once there are rows. It downloads the current result as a .csv file that you can open in Excel, Google Sheets, etc.

Images and files

  • PocketBase file fields — when the query selects from a collection (eg. SELECT * FROM posts), file columns are resolved to their real file URL and shown as clickable image cards (identical to the Collections table, including the preview modal). Your query must include the record id column for this to work (eg. SELECT * FROM posts rather than selecting only a few columns).
  • Image URLs / data URIs — any other value that looks like an image (a full URL, a relative path ending in an image extension, or a data:image/... URI) is shown as a thumbnail, with a text fallback if the image fails to load.

History

Your recently executed queries are stored locally in your browser (last 15) and can be re-run from the history menu (the clock icon in the page header). Click an entry to load it back into the editor, or use the small Clear link to remove an entry.

History is kept in your browser only — it is never sent to the server and is not shared with other users.

Syntax colors

The editor uses an SSMS-inspired color scheme to make queries easier to read:

Blue — keywords
Dark green — comments
Red — strings / text literals
Green — system schemas (sys, INFORMATION_SCHEMA)
Magenta — functions
Maroon — stored procedures (sp_*, xp_*)
Teal — line numbers and parameters
Dark gray — operators
Black on silver — SQLCMD commands

Safety and confirmations

  • Queries that may modify data or the schema — INSERT, UPDATE, DELETE, CREATE, DROP, ALTER, REPLACE — show a confirmation prompt before running.
  • Queries time out after 3 minutes.
  • Read-only SELECT queries run without a confirmation prompt.

Command cheat sheet

-- read data
SELECT * FROM posts;
SELECT id, title FROM posts WHERE views > 100 ORDER BY created DESC;

-- create a collection
CREATE TABLE notes (title TEXT, body EDITOR, done BOOL);

-- add / remove a field
ALTER TABLE notes ADD COLUMN priority SELECT(low, medium, high);
ALTER TABLE notes DROP COLUMN priority;

-- change data
INSERT INTO notes (title, body) VALUES ('Hello', 'World');
UPDATE notes SET done = true WHERE title = 'Hello';
DELETE FROM notes WHERE title = 'Hello';

-- list tables
SELECT name FROM sqlite_master WHERE type = 'table';

Troubleshooting

I cannot see the SQL Editor.
You are not logged in as a superuser. Log in with a superuser account.

My query runs but I do not see a table.
Only SELECT statements return a result table. INSERT / UPDATE / DELETE report the number of affected rows instead.

Only 250 rows are shown.
Click Load remaining at the bottom of the table. A maximum of 1000 rows is returned per query.

My image column shows raw text instead of a thumbnail.
Make sure the query selects from a real collection and includes the id column (eg. SELECT * FROM posts). File fields can only be resolved when the record id is known.

Ctrl+Z does nothing.
Click inside the editor first so it has focus, then use Ctrl+Z to undo and Ctrl+Y to redo.

What is the difference between SELECT and the other statements?
SELECT reads data and shows a table. All the other statements change data or the schema, and ask for confirmation first.
